In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WAS is an X-linked disorder of the immune system caused by mutation of the WAS protein (WASP) gene.
WAS is a complex disease, in which the immune deficiency, thrombo- and haemorrhagic diathesis, and the eczema are caused by a single genetic defect.

WAS is caused by mutations in the WAS gene, leading to the expression of a truncated WASp protein, which in turn causes defects in the actin polymerization and cell motility of haemopoietic and non-haemopoietic cells.

the WAS protein (WASp) is not only a key regulator of the actin cytoskeleton in haematopoietic cells [2], but is also a critical regulator of the immune synapse in lymphocytes [3].
